newsitem.title: USA: Boeing earned $254 million in fourth quarter.
newsitem.headline: Boeing earned $254 million in fourth quarter.

text.p: Boeing Co., the world's largest aircraft maker, said Thursday it earned $254 million in the fourth quarter, up from $218 million a year earlier.
The improved earnings, equal to 75 cents a share, came on revenue of $6.51 billion. A year earlier, Boeing earned 63 cents a share on sales of $4.5 billion.
Boeing, which last month agreed to buy rival McDonnell Douglas Corp., said its most recent results included income and revenue from Rockwell Corp., which was acquired Dec. 6.
Boeing attributed the increase in earnings to higher sales volume, though the company said that was offset in part by a higher tax rate. The 1995 period also included the effects of a 10-week strike.
The 1996 period included a charge of $84 million, or 21 cents a share, to fund an employee benefit trust.
Wall Street analysts had expected Boeing to report profits equal to 99 cents a share, according to First Call, which tracks brokerage earnings estimates.
For the year, Boeing earned $1.10 billion, or $3.19 a share, on sales of $22.68 billion. In 1995, the company earned $393 million, or $1.15 a share, on sales of $19.52 billion.
The Seattle-based company's 1995 income included a charge of $254 million, or 75 cents a share, to pay for a special retirment progrram.
Boeing Chairman Phil Condit said the company concluded the year with 717 new announced commercial airplane orders worth approximately $53 billion.
